author: ValWood
body:
Non coding RNA on the complementary strand to a known RNA (RNase P K-RNA) get GO annotation (via Rfam?

See
https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPNCRNA.7136


GO:0004526 | ribonuclease P activity | IEA with RF00009 | GO_REF:0000115

@blakesweeney
title: Rfam? RF00009 GO annotation provided for features on complementary strand

rename.to: Rfam? RF00009 GO annotation provided for features on complementary strand

author: blakesweeney
body: I think I know the cause. It looks like it comes from RNAcentral, where we run the Rfam analysis in forward and reverse direction on our sequences. While this is a good idea on genomes, it's not so good for RNAcentral's use case. We will need to fix our pipeline and rexport the data that gets picked up by GO. It shouldn't be a huge problem to do soonish.

body: Yeah all families were searched in forward and reverse direction which can lead to this issues when there is an ncRNA on the other strand. I'm going to try to rerun Rfam with the fix and create a new export which will not have these issues.

author: afg1
body:
The fix is in the upcoming release. 

I've searched the URS_taxids for those you put above and I don't see them in the new export. It's available here in preview if you need/want to check: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/RNAcentral/releases/.27.0/go_annotations/rnacentral_rfam_annotations.tsv.gz (expect that to be updated when we re-run export in a couple of days)

We're aiming to have it out by the end of next week/July. You can assign to me if you like.

author: ValWood
body: OK thanks! I have a local solution to block "GO:0006412 translation" at import, because I always annotate to more specific terms than this. so it is no longer bothering me. But I will remove the block when the issue is fixed.
